chapter: Publishing, Jelly Roll in Los Angeles and band lore
title: The murder of Woodman by his saxophonist son
summary: Spikes recounts how Woodman's son killed him at the door and injured his mother, and that he attended the funeral.

story.theme_name: Illness, injury and the deaths of colleagues
story.community_name: Illness, injury and death among jazz musicians

blocks.x: Yeah. You know about him gettin' murdered?
No!
Oh, my God!
When was that?

SPIKES - 159
Reel 5
Page 11

Here about four years ago, I think it is. The boy--the saxophone player, his son--he came home one night and knocked on the door, and Woodman opened the door, and he killed him. And he tried to kill his mother, and she run out of the yard, and they put him in...caught him and put him in jail for murder, and I think they sent him...must've sent him to the insane asylum 'cause I've never heard no more about it. But I was at his funeral. Woodman. And Paul...Paul...
Howard?
Howard and all of them was there.
That was the one known as Brother Woodman, right? The one they call Brother? 'Cause I know it wasn't Britt.
Britt's the trombone player... No, it was the little dark one, the saxophone player.
The one they call Brother. I don't know what his ...maybe he was William, Jr. I don't know.
Yeah. Yeah, he killed him. He opened the door, he started stabbing him...stabbing him, killed him. He killed him. Yeah, Woodman was a fine fellow. He was wonderful.
That's what I heard. I never knew him. I know Britt and Britt's wife.
He never did say anything about it?
No, he's a very quiet, reserved person.
Does he still play?
Oh, yes. He and his wife moved to New York just last year. They missed New York so they moved back there.

SPIKES - 160
Reel 5
Page 12
They were both good musicians. But this little brownskin one, the fat one, played saxophone. He's the one that killed him.
I did not know that. That is sad. I guess then that his wife is still living here. I mean...

I don't know if she... I think he...she crippled... fell and broke her leg or something trying to run from him or something like that but I don't know whether she's still living or not. I haven't heard from 'em since.
I talked to Britt when I was in the East last fall. I talked to him on the telephone.

I don't know what become of that other boy. I think they were going to send him to the insane asylum. They said he was crazy.

I told you about him.
